brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: 4 bases on one level (3 full and 1 half) with top covers on all four, open faces capped and joints bolted. 36 parts, and the final check found no collisions.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base piece:0,1,0;half-s

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 stands where bases (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet. The first corner tried was refused because the drawer fills it, so this is a different three-base corner.
platform-sm is fitted to the mount spike with setSpikeAccessory (a solid spike was refused, so I used a mount spike)

finish.summary: I built a single-level desk unit from four hex bases: three full bases at (0,0), (1,0) and (1,-1), plus a south half base at (0,1). A drawer sits on the half base's cut face. A mount spike stands where (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet and holds a small platform. My first choice of corner, (0,0)/(0,1)/(1,0), was refused because the drawer fills it (SPIKE_CLASH), so I added the (1,-1) base to make a second three-base corner. I also added top covers on all four bases as a desk surface, capped every open face and bolted the joints. The build has 36 parts. The final check reported no rule issues and no mesh collisions ("clear"). I added no props.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
